proposals.change: In train.py, add a parameter-free SquaredReLU module implementing square(ReLU(x)) and replace the Transformer MLP's GELU activation with it; preserve all dimensions and the 1,016,960-parameter count.
proposals.failure_signal: The hypothesis is falsified if paired held-out BPB gain is below 0.003, or if activation growth causes non-finite values, materially worse throughput, or increased peak memory.
proposals.hypothesis: Replacing GELU with squared ReLU will lower full-budget held-out BPB by approximately 0.008 because the sharper, superlinear positive-feature response should improve the expressivity and optimization efficiency of the fixed-width MLP.
proposals.interaction_risk: Low against the fixed parent because no previous proposals are queued; later changes to MLP width, initialization, normalization, or learning rate could alter squared ReLU's activation scale and effect.
proposals.mechanism: Squared ReLU keeps negative features gated while amplifying confident positive features, increasing the effective nonlinearity of each parameter-neutral feed-forward layer without changing attention, data order, or optimizer behavior.
proposals.resource_risk: No parameter or persistent-memory increase. ReLU plus squaring should have similar compute cost to GELU, with a small risk of larger activation or gradient magnitudes.
proposals.title: Squared-ReLU transformer MLP

proposals.change: In train.py, change ModelConfig.rope_base from 10,000.0 to 1,000.0; preserve all dimensions, interfaces, and the 1,016,960-parameter count.
proposals.failure_signal: Held-out BPB does not improve by at least 0.003, or optimization stability or throughput regresses beyond controller limits.
proposals.hypothesis: At the fixed 256-token context length, lowering the RoPE base to 1,000 will improve held-out BPB by giving more head dimensions position-varying phases over the usable context window.
proposals.interaction_risk: Independent of the queued Squared-ReLU proposal, though their combined BPB effects may not be additive if both alter how blocks use positional features.
proposals.mechanism: The lower base increases angular variation in RoPE's slower frequency bands, improving resolution of medium- and long-range token offsets within 256-token sequences without adding parameters.
proposals.resource_risk: Parameter- and activation-memory-neutral; negligible throughput impact because the same RoPE operations and tensor shapes are retained.
proposals.title: Short-context RoPE base 1,000

proposals.change: In train.py, replace parameter-free rotary position encoding with a learned 256-by-128 absolute position embedding, add it to token embeddings, remove the obsolete RoPE code/configuration, and update the enforced parameter count from 1,016,960 to 1,049,728 (within the 1,050,000 cap).
proposals.failure_signal: The candidate improves held-out BPB by less than 0.005, regresses BPB, or breaches controller throughput, memory, or stability gates.
proposals.hypothesis: For fixed 256-token TinyStories contexts, learned absolute position vectors will improve held-out BPB by at least 0.005 versus RoPE because the model can directly fit position-specific structure while using the remaining parameter allowance.
proposals.interaction_risk: Mutually exclusive with queued proposal 2, which changes the RoPE base; largely orthogonal to the queued Squared-ReLU proposal.
proposals.mechanism: The additional 32,768 learned values provide explicit, trainable position features and remove the need for the small model to express fixed-context positional regularities through rotary attention geometry alone.
proposals.resource_risk: Adds 32,768 parameters (3.2%) and small parameter, gradient, optimizer-state, and checkpoint memory overhead. Compute should remain roughly neutral because one embedding lookup replaces per-layer rotary transformations.
proposals.title: Learned absolute position embeddings

proposals.change: In train.py, RMS-normalize each attention head's query and key vectors across head_dim immediately after splitting heads and before applying RoPE; preserve all dimensions, interfaces, and the 1,016,960-parameter count.
proposals.failure_signal: The hypothesis is falsified if paired trials show less than 0.005 BPB gain, a BPB regression, instability, or a throughput or peak-memory regression beyond controller limits.
proposals.hypothesis: Parameter-free per-head query-key RMS normalization will lower full-budget held-out BPB by at least 0.005 by preventing poorly scaled attention logits during early and later training.
proposals.interaction_risk: Low. RMS normalization is independent of the queued MLP activation change and learned absolute-position proposal; because RoPE is norm-preserving, normalization before RoPE should also remain compatible with the queued RoPE-base change.
proposals.mechanism: Normalizing query and key vectors to consistent per-head RMS makes scaled dot-product logits less sensitive to projection magnitude drift, yielding more stable attention entropy and gradients while retaining directional information.
proposals.resource_risk: No parameter increase. Two additional per-head reductions and normalizations may slightly reduce throughput and retain modest extra query/key activations, so runtime and peak memory require controller measurement.
proposals.title: Parameter-free query-key RMS normalization

proposals.change: In train.py, replace the learned-scale, bias-free LayerNorm used before attention, before the MLP, and after the final block with parameter-neutral RMSNorm; preserve all dimensions, state-dict parameter names, interfaces, and the 1,016,960-parameter count.
proposals.failure_signal: The candidate fails to reduce held-out BPB by at least 0.005, becomes unstable, or incurs a material throughput or peak-memory regression.
proposals.hypothesis: RMSNorm will improve full-budget held-out BPB by at least 0.005 because retaining each residual stream's mean while controlling its RMS will preserve useful signal and stabilize scale throughout this small pre-normalized transformer.
proposals.interaction_risk: The benefit may overlap with queued query-key RMS normalization if that patch is later accepted; the queued activation and positional-encoding variants do not directly conflict, although their changed activation statistics could alter the effect size.
proposals.mechanism: Each normalization site rescales hidden states by their root-mean-square without subtracting the feature mean, maintaining residual-stream mean information while bounding activation magnitude and gradient scale.
proposals.resource_risk: Parameter count and persistent memory are unchanged. The explicit reduction and elementwise operations may be less fused than LayerNorm on some devices, causing a small throughput or temporary-memory regression.
proposals.title: Residual-stream RMSNorm

proposals.failure_signal: Paired held-out BPB gain is below 0.003, or stability or throughput materially regresses.

proposals.interaction_risk: Mutually exclusive with the queued Squared-ReLU MLP proposal; normalization changes may also alter gating dynamics.
proposals.mechanism: SiLU-activated gates multiplicatively select value features while retaining essentially the same projection parameter budget.
proposals.resource_risk: Trainable parameters decrease by 512; compute and peak activation memory should remain approximately unchanged, with a small possible elementwise throughput cost.
proposals.title: Near-parameter-matched SwiGLU MLP

proposals.failure_signal: Paired evaluation shows no held-out BPB improvement, or reduced embedding decay increases logit norms without improving held-out negative log-likelihood.

proposals.mechanism: The tied matrix serves simultaneously as the input lookup table and output classifier. Avoiding AdamW shrinkage prevents uniform erosion of its row norms while retaining regularization on attention and MLP matrices.
proposals.resource_risk: No parameter or activation-memory increase and negligible throughput impact; optimizer state size is unchanged because the same tensor merely moves between existing parameter groups.
proposals.title: No weight decay on tied embeddings

proposals.interaction_risk: Low; it is compatible with most queued architecture and optimizer proposals, but changes output-head state dictionaries and must be reconciled with patches that alter embeddings, logits, or the expected parameter count.
proposals.mechanism: The bias supplies a direct per-token prior, allowing the tied embedding matrix to focus more of its limited capacity on contextual representations and token compatibility.
proposals.resource_risk: Negligible: 1,792 additional parameters and one broadcast addition to logits, with no meaningful expected throughput or peak-memory change.
proposals.title: Learned vocabulary-logit bias

proposals.title: Zero-initialized transformer projection biases

proposals.resource_risk: No parameter increase; attention-score memory should decrease and throughput may improve slightly, though backend kernel efficiency for two heads could offset the gain.

proposals.failure_signal: Held-out BPB does not improve by at least 0.005, or late-training loss becomes worse as the lower learning rate reduces useful parameter updates.

proposals.mechanism: The unchanged cosine schedule now progressively suppresses update noise through the end of the fixed token budget, reducing late-stage oscillation around the converged solution.
proposals.resource_risk: Negligible; step count, optimizer state, throughput, peak memory, and parameter count are unchanged.
proposals.title: Cosine learning-rate decay to zero

proposals.interaction_risk: The effect may overlap with future changes to output-logit parameterization, embedding decay, normalization, or vocabulary bias; it is independently applicable to the supplied parent.
proposals.mechanism: Penalizing the squared log-sum-exp of valid-token logits discourages poorly conditioned logit offsets while leaving inference unchanged, potentially improving calibration and gradient stability.
proposals.resource_risk: No parameter or persistent-memory increase; one log-sum-exp reduction during training adds a small compute and temporary-memory cost.
proposals.title: Training-time logit z-loss

proposals.resource_risk: Parameter count and peak memory are unchanged, and throughput should be unchanged; larger updates introduce a modest stability risk.

proposals.mechanism: Each head learns multiplicative frequency adjustments in log space while retaining RoPE's relative-position structure. Zero initialization makes the starting model exactly equivalent to the parent, while 256 added scalars permit layer- and head-specific positional specialization.
proposals.resource_risk: Adds 256 parameters and only a small per-forward exponentiation over 64 values per layer; expected throughput and peak-memory impact are negligible. Static compilation passed, while train.py inspect could not run because the isolated environment lacked cached dependencies.
proposals.title: Per-head learnable RoPE frequencies

proposals.change: In train.py, change the training CLI default --weight-decay from 0.1 to 0.01 while preserving optimizer grouping, architecture, interfaces, token budgets, and the 1,016,960-parameter count.
proposals.failure_signal: The full-budget paired trial improves held-out BPB by less than 0.003, is neutral or worse, or exhibits a larger train-to-dev generalization gap consistent with insufficient regularization.
proposals.hypothesis: Because the fixed 20M-token budget leaves this 1M-parameter model undertrained, reducing AdamW weight decay from 0.1 to 0.01 will avoid excessive shrinkage of learned matrices and lower held-out BPB by at least 0.003.
proposals.interaction_risk: The effect may weaken if the queued no-decay-on-tied-embeddings proposal is accepted, because that removes weight decay from the model's largest shared matrix; it may also depend on accepted learning-rate or batch-size changes.
proposals.mechanism: Tenfold weaker decoupled weight decay lets attention, MLP, and tied embedding weights retain more task-relevant magnitude during the short fixed-budget optimization while keeping modest regularization on matrix parameters.
proposals.resource_risk: Negligible throughput and peak-memory impact; the optimizer operations, state size, parameter count, and training schedule are unchanged.
proposals.title: Reduce AdamW weight decay to 0.01

proposals.change: In train.py, add a zero-initialized learned scalar logit_scale, multiply vocabulary logits by exp(logit_scale), and update EXPECTED_PARAMETER_COUNT from 1,016,960 to 1,016,961.
proposals.failure_signal: Paired full-budget held-out BPB improves by less than 0.003, regresses, or the learned scale remains effectively 1.0 throughout training.
proposals.hypothesis: A directly learned global logit temperature will improve held-out BPB by at least 0.003 by calibrating prediction sharpness independently of the tied embedding matrix.
proposals.interaction_risk: The effect may overlap with queued output-bias, low-rank output-adapter, embedding weight-decay, or z-loss proposals; it is independently applicable to the fixed parent.
proposals.mechanism: The scalar supplies a low-cost calibration degree of freedom, allowing cross-entropy to adjust overall softmax confidence without changing token geometry or globally rescaling the tied input/output embeddings.
proposals.resource_risk: Negligible throughput and memory impact: one trainable scalar, one exponential per forward pass, and one elementwise logit multiplication.
proposals.title: Learned global logit temperature

proposals.change: In train.py, add an identity-initialized, bias-free, kernel-size-3 causal depthwise convolution to each attention layer's value projection before splitting heads, and update EXPECTED_PARAMETER_COUNT from 1,016,960 to 1,018,496.
proposals.failure_signal: The hypothesis is falsified if paired evaluation shows less than 0.005 BPB improvement, instability, or a controller-rejected throughput or memory regression.
proposals.hypothesis: Giving each attention value channel a learnable causal three-token receptive field will improve held-out BPB by exposing reusable local phrase features while preserving the baseline function at initialization.
proposals.interaction_risk: This may overlap with queued proposal 21's MLP depthwise convolution because both add local token mixing; effects may not combine additively if that proposal is accepted.
proposals.mechanism: The identity-initialized convolution initially copies each value unchanged, then can learn channel-specific mixtures of the current and two preceding value vectors before global causal attention routes them.
proposals.resource_risk: Adds 1,536 parameters and one small grouped convolution per layer. Peak memory should change minimally, but convolution launches and transposes may modestly reduce throughput.
proposals.title: Causal depthwise convolution on attention values

proposals.change: In train.py, replace the learned-scale-only LayerNorms before attention, before the MLP, and after the final block with fully affine LayerNorms by adding zero-initialized 128-channel biases; update EXPECTED_PARAMETER_COUNT from 1,016,960 to 1,018,112.
proposals.failure_signal: The paired full-budget candidate shows less than 0.002 BPB gain, no gain, or worse BPB relative to the parent.
proposals.hypothesis: Learned LayerNorm offsets will lower held-out BPB by at least 0.002 because the bias-free projections currently cannot independently learn normalized activation mean shifts.
proposals.interaction_risk: The effect may be redundant with projection-bias or vocabulary-logit-bias proposals, and it conflicts structurally with replacing LayerNorm by RMSNorm.
proposals.mechanism: Zero-initialized biases preserve the parent's initial function while allowing each pre-normalized residual branch and the final normalized representation to learn channel-wise offsets, increasing representational flexibility with minimal parameters.
proposals.resource_risk: Adds 1,152 parameters (about 0.11%) while remaining below the cap; throughput and peak-memory impact should be negligible.
proposals.title: Fully affine LayerNorm
